narrative: Material PL1__M82D44A4 exhibits smooth demand patterns with moderate variability (CV=0.49) and a statistically significant declining trend (p<0.001). Historical data shows 140 working-day observations with 5 outliers detected (including 2 extreme lead time data errors >9000 days). After data cleaning and winsorisation, mean daily demand is 347.2 units with standard deviation 169.3. Lead time analysis reveals moderate stability (CV=0.39) with mean 4.0 days (±1.6 days). Variance decomposition shows lead time variability dominates (72% of total uncertainty), driving safety stock requirements. The optimized (r,Q) policy recommends safety stock of 1052 units and order quantity of 3152 units (capacity-constrained from EOQ of 5289 units), yielding a reorder point of 2452 units. This policy achieves 95% service level while reducing total annual costs by $1660 (27.5%) compared to the current SAP baseline.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Selected continuous review model based on smooth demand regime (CV=0.49, non-zero fraction=97.9%), high observation count (n=140), and moderate lead time variability. Normal approximation justified by central limit theorem given sufficient sample size and distribution kurtosis (-0.51) within acceptable range. Capacity constraint (4204 units) binds the order quantity below unconstrained EOQ.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Primary risk stems from declining demand trend (slope=-1.23 units/period, p=0.0004), which may reduce optimal order quantities over time. Lead time variability (CV=0.39) contributes 72% of safety stock uncertainty. Zero-demand periods observed (2.1% of observations) suggest potential intermittent behavior if trend continues. Capacity constraint may limit responsiveness to demand spikes. Recommend quarterly policy review given trend significance.
